intersections.note: Miller Pl. (25 ft) runs south from Fairmount to Knox. Fairmount is only 20 ft wide west of Liddell
Liddell (LIDDELL, no suffix) comes in diagonally from the north-west at the top edge and ends at Fairmount; Fairmount widens to 50 ft east of here

Fairmount ends at the north-south street along the railroad. That street is unlabelled on this stretch; BEEKMAN is printed only on its diagonal south of Knox. It runs on north off the top edge and is labelled Western Av. on sheet 514, so this is the same crossing as Western Avenue / Fairmount Avenue there
Bloom (45 ft) starts at Knox and runs south-south-west
Knox ends at Beekman (Cincinnati Screw & Tap Co. opposite)
same crossing as on sheet 511; Lawnway starts here and runs south
Bloom ends at Waverly (Lunkenheimer works opposite)

same crossing as on sheet 511. Queen City's south line is off the bottom of the paper here; centre taken on the 10 in. water pipe, about 30 ft south of the north line. This corner sits in the binding fold
a street continues south-south-west from the south side of Queen City onto sheet 504 (block corners at x 1705 and 1975), slightly west of Beekman's line

widths.note: 20 ft printed at the west edge; 50 ft printed east of Liddell near Beekman
50 ft printed at Waverly, 42 ft just north of Tremont, 45 ft south of Tremont

alleys.note: block between Knox and Waverly; continues from sheet 511 (where it crosses Quince Alley) and ends at Bloom
stub west from Miller Pl. between Fairmount and Knox; dead-ends at a lot line

bends.note: Beekman runs due north from here to Fairmount and beyond; south of here it is a straight diagonal to Queen City

notes: Single panel. Fairmount Av. along the top (20 ft west of Liddell, 50 ft east of it), Knox (50 ft), Waverly Av. (50 ft), Tremont (50 ft) and Queen City Av. (60 ft) at the bottom. Lawnway (LAWNWAY, no suffix) down the left edge in the binding fold, from Waverly to Queen City (overlap with sheet 511). Miller Pl. Fairmount to Knox. Bloom from Knox south to Waverly. Beekman (60 ft) is a straight diagonal from Queen City north-north-east to about y 1590, then runs due north past Fairmount off the top edge (Western Av. on sheet 514); the north-south stretch carries no name on this sheet. The dash-dot line near the left edge marked C (at Fairmount) and B (at Knox) is a boundary line, not a street. Right half: C.H.&D. railroad, brick yard and vacant lots, no streets except Queen City. A curved railroad spur in the Lunkenheimer block is ignored.
